statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 19 sits in the low band, below the block threshold, while Stress 67 remains high on the rates and energy backdrop.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow danger window spans 12:30 to 14:30 UTC, covering the bundled US release block at 12:30, the 13:30 cash open and 14:00 pending home sales, where the conditional readings of this cycle are highest.
headline: NQ holds 29,456.75, still capped beneath a five-hour-old 29,477.00 overnight high; Tail steady at 19 while Stress eases to 67 with crude flat near $102.38
body:
The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3-3/4 to 4 percent at 18:00 UTC on 16 September in a unanimous 12-0 vote, the first increase in more than three years, and the accompanying projections show a majority of officials expecting one further increase this year. Chair Warsh framed the decision around inflation that has not clearly returned to target.

Cash markets closed split on 16 September. The Nasdaq-100 finished at 28,945.06, up 0.02 percent, inside a 28,753.29 to 29,235.89 day range, while the Dow fell about 1.2 percent and the S&P 500 about 0.44 percent. Index-level tech absorbed the decision far better than the rate-sensitive cyclical complex, which is a rotation signature rather than a broad de-risking one.

Overnight, futures have recovered. NQ trades at 29,456.75, up 0.68 percent, inside a 29,247.75 to 29,477.00 range. The decisive structural fact is that the 29,477.00 high was set roughly five hours ago and has not been taken out since: the recovery leg has repeatedly failed to extend, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the Tail measure is designed to detect. Cross-assets are consistent with that reading. The ten-year yield sits at 5.01 percent, essentially unchanged after the decision, WTI is near $102.38 and Brent near $105.89 as Saudi Arabia signals a partial East-West pipeline restart within days, and the VIX is near 17.7.

Tail is therefore held at 19, in the low band. Price sitting close to a session extreme is the single mild amplifier and is why the reading is not lower; the repeated failure to extend, the orderly post-event price discovery, the flat curve response and the easing energy premium are why it is not higher. Stress eases to 67, still high, because a hiking Fed, a five percent ten-year and triple-digit crude remain a demanding environment even when the price path is orderly. Confidence is 86 on live futures, yield, crude and volatility levels and a calendar verified against the Federal Reserve's own September schedule; the shared Finviz cross-asset context was stale and partial at run time and was not relied upon.

The narrow danger window spans 12:30 to 14:30 UTC, covering the bundled 12:30 release block of jobless claims, housing starts, building permits and the Philadelphia Fed index, the 13:30 cash open and 14:00 pending home sales. Those are the checkpoints where the conditional readings of this cycle peak, at 22 and 23, and they are conditional estimates rather than assertions that post-release continuation has been observed.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding Claude clock-hours are available from published history and none has been restated with later information. The cycle opened in the low band at 14 to 16 with a normal dominant mode through the Asian and European sessions of 16 September. It entered the watch band at 12:00 UTC with the US pre-market and held 20 to 22 through the early afternoon, reaching 24 in the 18:00 UTC statement hour. The single orange print came at 19:00 UTC, Tail 31 with a trend-down mode, during the press conference and the yield extension to five percent. It fell back to 20 within an hour and to 18 and 16 by 21:00 and 22:00 UTC as the post-event path proved orderly. The overnight recovery lifted the reading back to 20 at 00:00 and 01:00 UTC with a trend-up mode, then settled to 19 with a mixed mode in the two hours before this assessment as the advance stalled beneath its high.
outlookSummary: The forecast opens at 19 for the current hour, the only slot backed by observed price-path structure, then eases to 18 through the thin pre-European stretch as the post-decision leg ages further out of its efficient window. It firms back to 19 from the 07:00 UTC European cash open and holds there through the European morning, where continental desks price the hike and a five percent ten-year. The 11:00 to 15:00 UTC slots carry the highest conditional readings at 20, 22, 23, 21 and 20, spanning the bundled 12:30 UTC release block, the 13:30 UTC cash open and 14:00 UTC pending home sales; these are conditional event readings, not assertions that post-release continuation has been observed. The reading returns to 19 across the US afternoon, firms to 20 for the power hour into the 20:00 UTC close, and decays to an 18 plateau across the maintenance break, the futures reopen and the following Asian session, where no catalyst is scheduled. Stress declines gradually from 67 to 65 and confidence from 86 to 75 as the horizon lengthens.
